refranes: Kiddo, whoever saves even a little at a time never wakes up to cryin' pockets.
Don't spend the whole harvest today, sugar. You never know when a hard drought's comin'.
The money you look after today is what keeps you from beggin' favors tomorrow.
Don't buy things so folks will look at you. Buy 'em 'cause you truly need 'em.
It ain't how much you save, mijo. It's gettin' in the habit of savin'.
Folks who know how to handle money never end up broke as a church mouse.
Chargin' what you're owed ain't stingy. It's respectin' the sweat on your brow.
If you did the work, then you get paid, pues. Hard work don't come on credit.
Don't be shy about chargin'. What's shameful is workin' and then waitin' on your money.
When you value your own time, darlin', other folks learn to value it too.
Bein' good people don't mean givin' your work away.
Anybody who truly values what you do pays without you havin' to beg.
Listen here, kiddo: clear accounts keep friendships whole.
What's collected on time don't end up in a fight.
Don't give away what cost you so much sweat and a sore back to earn.
Savin' builds the house; bein' careless with money tears it down.
You ain't rich by what you make, but by what you manage to keep.
Money well looked after works real quiet while you sleep.
¡Ave María!, charge with respect, but charge. The one who keeps quiet ends up losin'.
Learn two things in this life, darlin': put money away when you've got it, and charge what's yours without shame. Do that, and half your life's already squared away.
